posts.title: One page beats nine: what an EPK is actually for
posts.excerpt: An A&R gives the email forty seconds on a phone between sessions. One page with three links survives that; a nine-page PDF does not, and the same rule sells a beat pack.

posts.title: Ear, range and timing: curation as a producer's real career asset
posts.excerpt: Three hundred and sixty releases in, track output is the cheapest thing in the catalogue. The ear, the range and the timing behind the picks are what buyers, sync desks and festivals actually pay for.

posts.title: Cross-collateralisation and the missing Record One clause
posts.excerpt: The streams did the numbers and the royalty ledger still reads zero, because the producer points wait behind every cost the deal can reach. One clause decides which paper you signed.

posts.title: Paid two periods in arrears: how a producer actually gets paid off a placement
posts.excerpt: The streams start on release weekend. The money starts on the label's accounting calendar, which runs months behind by design.

posts.title: The pocket doesn't fit in a prompt: what an AI beat generator can't hold
posts.excerpt: A prompt is a description; a beat is a set of decisions at resolutions a description can't reach. What breaks first: step-level timing, a vocalist who hasn't turned up, and a sound with a name instead of a category.

posts.title: Loud isn't big: density vs size in a mix
posts.excerpt: Two records can tie on the meter and still differ in size. Perceived loudness gets bought with contrast and density, size gets bought with space, and the order you buy them in decides what survives the master.

posts.title: Log drums, pushed kicks and one swing setting: what makes a beat read as its genre
posts.excerpt: A type beat's tag is a promise the first bar has to keep. The exact moves that make a beat read as amapiano, dancehall or UK garage, and which of them survive being played badly.

posts.title: Two copyrights, one sample: what clears and what it costs when you get it wrong
posts.excerpt: Every sample sits behind two doors: the master and the publishing. What clearing both actually involves, and what an uncleared chop costs once Content ID finds it.

posts.title: The One Drum Hit That Defines Afroswing
posts.excerpt: Move the snare one beat and a UK rap record becomes an Afroswing record. Here's the displacement that built a genre, and how to program it.
